source.title: Additional programs verified from official and directory pages
source.note: Facts taken from the cited pages. Phone numbers are included only where the cited source showed them.

records.name: Utah Independent Living Center
records.description: Center for Independent Living serving Salt Lake, Summit and Tooele counties. Utah's first independent living center, open since 1982.
records.next_step: Call and ask about independent living services, assistive technology and home accessibility help, and whether they can help with a ramp or modification request.
constraints: Services and funding for modifications vary by center and year. Ask what is available now.

records.name: Roads to Independence
records.description: Center for Independent Living in Ogden serving Morgan, Weber and Davis counties.
records.next_step: Call and ask about independent living services, assistive technology and home accessibility help, and whether they can help with a ramp or modification request.
constraints: Services and funding for modifications vary by center and year. Ask what is available now.

records.name: Ability 1st
records.description: Center for Independent Living in Provo serving Juab, Sanpete, Utah and Wasatch counties.
records.next_step: Call and ask about independent living services, assistive technology and home accessibility help, and whether they can help with a ramp or modification request.
constraints: Services and funding for modifications vary by center and year. Ask what is available now.

records.name: Active Re-Entry
records.description: Center for Independent Living serving seven eastern Utah counties from offices in Price, Moab and Vernal.
records.next_step: Call and ask about independent living services, assistive technology and home accessibility help, and whether they can help with a ramp or modification request.
constraints: Services and funding for modifications vary by center and year. Ask what is available now.

records.name: Red Rock Center for Independence (RRCI)
records.description: Center for Independent Living in St. George serving nine southwestern and central Utah counties.
records.next_step: Look up current contact details in the ILRU directory, then call and ask about independent living and home accessibility help.
constraints: Services and funding for modifications vary by center and year. Ask what is available now.

records.name: Options for Independence
records.description: Center for Independent Living in Logan (northern Utah).
records.next_step: Look up current contact details in the ILRU directory, then call and ask whether your county is in its service area.
constraints: Counties served are not listed here. Ask whether your address is in its service area.

records.name: Utah Assistive Technology Foundation low-interest loans
records.org: Utah Assistive Technology Program / Utah Assistive Technology Foundation
records.description: Low-interest loans, made with Zions Bank through the Utah Assistive Technology Foundation, for devices such as wheelchairs, scooters, lifts, adapted vans and home modifications. Small grants are also described for people at or below 150% of the federal poverty line.
records.next_step: Call UATP, read the application instructions and ask what documents you need, such as an invoice with model and price.
constraints: Loan approval depends on credit, debts and income. Confirm current rates and grant rules with the program.

records.name: Utah Assistive Technology Program device reuse and loan closet
records.description: Refurbished wheelchairs, walkers, ramps, lifts and other equipment sold, loaned or rented, with locations in Logan, the Uintah Basin and Salt Lake City, plus the statewide AT4All swap site. Posted rental rates include transportable folding ramps and wheelchairs.
records.next_step: Call and ask what is in stock, current rental or purchase prices, and whether you can try the device before committing.
constraints: Prices and stock change. Confirm before you travel.

records.name: Adaptive Modifications Program (Philadelphia)
records.description: Free accessibility changes such as ramps, lifts, widened doorways and accessible bathrooms for Philadelphia residents with a permanent physical disability. Homeowners, and renters with the owner's permission, may apply.
records.next_step: Contact PHDC, ask for the Adaptive Modifications Program application, and ask about the current wait time and income rules.
constraints: Home must be structurally sound and the disability permanent. Funding limits and waits apply; confirm current rules.
records.phone_note: PHDC, 1234 Market Street, 17th Floor, Philadelphia, PA 19107. Use the program page for the current phone number.

records.name: Senior Housing Assistance Repair Program (SHARP)
records.description: Minor home repairs and modifications such as grab bars and railings for income-eligible Philadelphia homeowners age 60 and over.
records.next_step: Contact the Philadelphia Corporation for Aging and ask about SHARP eligibility and the waiting list.
constraints: Age 60 or over, income-eligible homeowners with a structurally sound home.

records.name: Adaptive modifications (Chester County)
records.description: Grant-funded adaptive modifications such as ramps, lifts, door and hallway widening and bathroom or kitchen changes for eligible Chester County residents with disabilities. Repayment is not required.
records.next_step: Open the PA 211 listing, read the eligibility details and use the intake link to apply.
constraints: Eligibility and funding limits apply. Confirm on the listing.

records.name: OOD home modifications and vehicle modification
records.description: Ohio vocational rehabilitation can fund home modifications and vehicle modifications when they are needed to reach an employment goal. State rules cover both services.
records.next_step: Apply to OOD vocational rehabilitation and tell your counselor which modification you need and why it supports work.
constraints: Tied to an employment goal and an OOD plan. Not a general home repair program. Approval comes before work starts.
records.phone_note: Use the OOD website to find your local office.

records.name: Kettering Accessibility Modification Grants
records.description: City grants of up to $10,000 for income-eligible Kettering homeowners who need to modify a home because of a disability, such as adding a ramp or step.
records.next_step: Contact the City of Kettering housing programs and ask for the current Accessibility Modification Grant application and income limits.
constraints: City of Kettering residents only. Grant amounts and funding change; confirm with the city.

records.name: Modcon Living Safe at Home (Franklin County)
records.org: Modcon Living (formerly Rebuilding Together Central Ohio)
records.description: Free emergency repairs and home modifications for low-income senior, disabled and veteran homeowners in Franklin County.
records.next_step: Contact Modcon Living and ask for the Safe at Home application and current waitlist.
constraints: Listed in a third-party directory that says it did not confirm the program. Check with the organization directly.

records.name: OPWDD assistive technology, environmental and vehicle modifications
records.org: NY Office for People With Developmental Disabilities (OPWDD)
records.description: People enrolled in the OPWDD Comprehensive Waiver can request home modifications such as a ramp to the front door or a roll-in shower, plus adaptive devices and vehicle modifications. Vehicle work must be done by a NMEDA-accredited installer.
records.next_step: Ask your Care Manager to prepare the request for OPWDD review using the state guidance and review sheet.
constraints: Requires OPWDD waiver enrollment. Requests go through a care manager and an approval process.

records.name: Medicaid environmental modification guidelines
records.description: State guidelines describe how home accessibility modifications, such as ramps, are authorized for Medicaid participants under Community First Choice Option services.
records.next_step: Ask your Medicaid care manager or plan how to request an environmental modification assessment and which provider to use.
constraints: Authorization rules apply and service limits are tied to medical necessity.

records.name: People Inc. Environmental Modifications (EMods)
records.description: Helps people qualified for OPWDD services plan and complete home modifications, assistive technology and vehicle modifications, including guiding families through the OPWDD approval process.
records.next_step: Open the EMods page and use its link to ask whether you qualify.
constraints: For people qualified for OPWDD services. Service area may extend beyond Erie County; ask.

records.name: Free modular ramp program (Oswego and Cayuga)
records.description: Builds and installs free modular wheelchair ramps for eligible people in Oswego and Cayuga counties, listed in a Central New York health resource directory.
records.next_step: Call the county contact and ask about eligibility and the current ramp waitlist.
constraints: Oswego line shown; the Cayuga contact is 315-255-3447. Eligibility rules apply.

records.name: Regional centers (21 nonprofit agencies)
records.description: Regional centers coordinate and purchase services for Californians with developmental disabilities, including assessments, eligibility decisions and case management. Ask your service coordinator about equipment and home accessibility.
records.next_step: Use the state regional center lookup to find your center, then ask about eligibility and an Individual Program Plan meeting.
constraints: Eligibility is for qualifying developmental disabilities. Regional centers purchase services only after other funding is explored.

records.name: Rebuilding Together affiliate finder (home repair and modifications)
records.description: National nonprofit with local affiliates that provide free home repairs and accessibility modifications, often ramps, grab bars and railings, for low-income homeowners, especially older adults, people with disabilities and veterans. Programs include Safe at Home.
records.next_step: Use the affiliate finder, call the one that covers your address and ask whether it takes accessibility projects and how long the wait is.
constraints: Services differ by affiliate. Wait times vary and many affiliates have limited funding.

records.name: Access to Home Program (New York City)
records.org: New York Foundation for Senior Citizens
records.description: Home modifications for New York City residents age 18 or older with substantial physical limitations, homeowners or renters, funded by the state housing agency. Modifications include ramps, handrails and accessible bathrooms.
records.next_step: Call or email the program and ask about eligibility, income limits and the application.
constraints: Low and moderate income applicants. Renters and condo or co-op owners need extra documents. State funding is limited, so ask about waits.

records.name: Accessibility Upgrades Program (New York City)
records.description: Home accessibility help listed by New York City for people with disabilities, including ramps, lifts, handrails and lever door handles, for homeowners or renters.
records.next_step: Call and ask about eligibility and the current wait.
constraints: Eligibility rules apply. Confirm with the organization.

records.name: Access to Home, Doorways to Independence (New York City)
records.description: Home modification program for people with disabilities listed by New York City as operated by Adapt Community Network.
records.next_step: Call and ask about eligibility and how to apply.
constraints: Eligibility rules apply. Confirm with the organization.

records.name: Home maintenance and modification services (Allegheny County)
records.description: Free home repairs and accessibility modifications for low-income Allegheny County homeowners. Older adults, veterans and people with permanent disabilities are priorities.
records.next_step: Call or visit the office at 7800 Susquehanna Street, Suite 102, Pittsburgh, and ask how to apply.
constraints: PA 211 lists income below 150% of the federal poverty guidelines, current real estate taxes and owner occupancy. Confirm with the organization.
records.phone_note: Use the PA 211 listing for the current phone number.

records.name: Allegheny County Whole-Home Repairs Program
records.description: Repairs and accessibility modifications for eligible Allegheny County homeowners, including ramps, grab bars, handrails, doorway widening and bathroom changes.
records.next_step: Open the program page and use the application link.
constraints: Funding rounds open and close. Check whether applications are open.

records.name: Home Accessibility Program for Independence
records.description: City of Pittsburgh program that helps residents with physical disabilities remain in their homes.
records.next_step: Read the program page and ask the URA to notify you when the next round opens.
constraints: The page says applications closed July 31, 2026. Check for the next round.

records.name: Rebuilding Together Northeast Ohio
records.description: Free home repairs for low-income homeowners in Northeast Ohio, including Cleveland, with ramps listed among the work. Seniors, people with disabilities and veterans are priorities.
records.next_step: Call and ask whether they build ramps in your area and how long the wait is.
constraints: Listed in a third-party directory that did not confirm the program. Check with the organization.

records.name: People Working Cooperatively home repair and modification
records.description: Home repair and accessibility modifications for older, low-income homeowners and people with disabilities in the Cincinnati area.
records.next_step: Call and ask about eligibility and the current waitlist.
constraints: Listed in the national Home Modification directory. Phone may be a program line; confirm service area.

records.name: Minor Home Repair Program (Franklin County)
records.description: County program that has installed wheelchair ramps for residents. A 2022 news report described an eight to twelve week waitlist.
records.next_step: Call the Office on Aging and ask about eligibility and the current waitlist.
constraints: Based on a 2022 news report. Confirm eligibility and current wait times.

records.name: Rental Housing Accessibility Program (Chico)
records.org: Independent Living Services of Northern California
records.description: Home accessibility help for renters with disabilities in the Chico area.
records.next_step: Call and ask about eligibility and the application.
constraints: Listed in the national Home Modification directory. Confirm service area and current funding.

records.name: Community Living Fund (assistive technology and home modifications)
records.description: A state initiative described as funding assistive technology, durable medical equipment and home modifications through partner nonprofits.
records.next_step: Open the Department of Rehabilitation page and ask your local independent living center whether the fund is open.
constraints: Described in an AT Act initiative listing. Confirm current availability.

records.name: USOR Independent Living program
records.description: State independent living program that works with the independent living centers. Its forms cover home installation agreements, independent living plans and vehicle modification agreements.
records.next_step: Ask your independent living center or the state office about an independent living plan and what equipment or home installation it can fund.
constraints: Program policy excludes some items, such as vehicle chassis. Funding is limited.

records.name: Utah Center for Assistive Technology vehicle modifications
records.description: State assistive technology center that evaluates and modifies vehicles, such as hand controls and wheelchair lifts for vans.
records.next_step: Call and ask how to get a vehicle evaluation and whether a vocational rehabilitation counselor must refer you.
constraints: Listed in a provider directory. Eligibility rules apply.

records.name: Repair Program (Utah County)
records.org: Habitat for Humanity of Utah County
records.description: Home repair program for low-income homeowners in Utah County.
records.next_step: Call and ask whether the program takes accessibility work such as ramps.
constraints: Listed in the national Home Modification directory. Confirm what repairs it covers.

records.name: Vocational rehabilitation equipment and home modification
records.description: Vocational rehabilitation can buy equipment and vehicle modifications tied to a work goal. A state bid notice showed it can also seek contractors for a customer's home modification.
records.next_step: Contact your local Texas Workforce Solutions office and ask for a vocational rehabilitation counselor.
constraints: Tied to an employment goal and a VR plan. Approval comes before work starts.

records.name: Independent Living Services
records.description: State independent living services can include home modifications such as wheelchair ramps, stair lifts and grab bars, plus vehicle modifications.
records.next_step: Open the program page and use the contact route to ask about eligibility and applying.
constraints: Eligibility rules apply. Funding is limited.

records.name: Texas Ramps
records.description: Provides free wheelchair ramps to disabled or elderly people who cannot afford one. Most referrals come from case workers and are submitted online.
records.next_step: Ask your case worker or social worker to submit the online referral.
constraints: Listed in a senior directory. Service area varies. Confirm before relying on it.

records.name: Illinois Assistive Technology Program loans
records.description: Loans for Illinois residents with disabilities to buy equipment and services tied to the disability, including home modifications. The program also runs a home modification loan.
records.next_step: Call IATP and ask about current loan types, amounts and how to apply.
constraints: Loan limits and rates change. Confirm with the program.

records.name: Illinois DHS Home Modification Program
records.description: State program to help people with disabilities pay for home modifications. The state grant listing says it serves people not already served by the Home Services Program.
records.next_step: Call the Home Services Program line and ask whether you qualify for the Home Modification Program or Home Services environmental modifications.
constraints: Rules and funding limits apply. Confirm current eligibility with the department.
records.phone_note: Main line for the Home Services Program, listed in the City of Chicago funding guide.

records.name: FODAC equipment reuse (Stone Mountain)
records.org: Friends of Disabled Adults and Children (FODAC)
records.description: Nonprofit that accepts donated durable medical equipment, repairs and refurbishes it, and distributes it for reuse. It operates most of Georgia's equipment reuse program with Tools for Life.
records.next_step: Look up the Tools for Life funding page, then contact FODAC and ask what is in stock and how to apply.
constraints: Stock changes. Ask about eligibility and cost.

records.name: Assistive work technology: home and vehicle modifications
records.description: Rehabilitation engineers and technologists work with vocational rehabilitation counselors on home modifications, vehicle modifications and evaluations for clients.
records.next_step: Contact the agency and ask about a vocational rehabilitation application.
constraints: Tied to a vocational rehabilitation plan and employment goal.
records.phone_note: Contact line from an agency flyer for agricultural workers. Use the agency site for your local office.

records.name: NCATP Equipment Exchange and Reuse Program
records.description: Connects North Carolina residents with gently used assistive technology and durable medical equipment, and lets people donate, offer or sell equipment through the NCATP Exchange.
records.next_step: Call the program, ask what is available, and use the Exchange form to post or request equipment.
constraints: Availability varies.

records.name: Independent Living Rehabilitation Program
records.org: NC Division of Vocational Rehabilitation Services
records.description: State program that helps people with disabilities live more independently. The state lists it among public programs that may build ramps or know of other ramp builders.
records.next_step: Call the nearest office and ask about eligibility and ramp or home modification help.
constraints: Each program has its own criteria. Listing is from a 2018 state ramp resource sheet and a county guide.
records.phone_note: Durham office also listed at 919-650-6810.

records.name: Ramp construction and assistive equipment loan
records.org: United Cerebral Palsy of Metropolitan Detroit
records.description: Listed by a Michigan aging network directory as offering ramp construction and an assistive equipment loan for Michigan residents with disabilities. The person who needs the equipment, or family, applies.
records.next_step: Call and ask about ramp eligibility, cost and the current wait.
constraints: Directory listing. The office is in Southfield; confirm its service area and current programs.
records.phone_note: Southfield office.

records.name: Handyworker Program (City of Los Angeles)
records.description: Free minor home repairs and accessibility improvements, including ramps, grab bars and handrails, for low-income seniors and people with permanent disabilities in the City of Los Angeles. Homeowners can receive up to $5,000 for modifications.
records.next_step: Open the program page, check the income limits and apply.
constraints: City of Los Angeles only. Income limits apply.

records.name: Home Improvement Program (Torrance)
records.description: Free home improvement services for Torrance residents who are people with disabilities or seniors and meet program criteria.
records.next_step: Open the program page, gather proof of home ownership and submit the application.
constraints: Torrance residents only.

records.name: Senior Grant Program (unincorporated Los Angeles County)
records.description: Home barrier removal and rehabilitation grants for low-income homeowners age 62 and over in unincorporated areas of Los Angeles County supervisorial districts 1, 2, 4 and 5.
records.next_step: Open the 211 listing and ask LACDA about the current application.
constraints: Age 62+, about 80% of area median income or less, owner-occupied.

records.name: Ohio Home Care Waiver vehicle modification
records.description: The Ohio Home Care Waiver can pay for vehicle modification when the state authorizes it. State rules list the driver and vehicle documents needed before approval.
records.next_step: If you are on the Ohio Home Care Waiver, ask your case manager about a vehicle modification request.
constraints: Requires enrollment in the waiver and prior authorization.

records.name: Free volunteer-built Toddler Mobility Trainer
records.description: MakeGood is a nonprofit that connects volunteer makers with children who need custom mobility and adaptive equipment. Its open-source 3D-printed Toddler Mobility Trainer, a pediatric wheelchair-style device for ages 1 to 8, can be requested free through the MakeGood Network.
records.next_step: Use the request page to ask for a volunteer-built chair for your child, and expect a waitlist.
constraints: For young children (ages 1 to 8); free requests may involve a waitlist.
Designs are open source, so you can also build or repair one yourself.

records.name: Open-source adaptive device designs
records.description: MakeGood publishes free, open-source designs for assistive devices that anyone with a consumer 3D printer can make. Files are hosted on Bambu Lab MakerWorld. A 3D-printed Toddler Mobility Trainer costs about $150 to produce.
records.next_step: Browse MakeGood designs, or contact MakeGood to ask about a custom adaptive device.
constraints: Printing and assembly are done by you or a volunteer maker; confirm fit and safety with your therapist.

records.name: The Wheelchair Repair Shop
records.description: A new program of Oregon Spinal Cord Injury Connection that provides wheelchair maintenance and repair in Portland using trained volunteers. It grew out of earlier wheelchair maintenance workshops and repair nights.
records.next_step: Check oregonsci.org for repair shop hours and what to bring before you visit.
constraints: Starting in Portland; confirm hours, location and which repairs are offered.

records.name: Nick Feldman Wheelchair and Mobility Device Repair Program
records.org: Independent Living Resource Center San Francisco
records.description: Repairs wheelchairs, scooters, walkers and other mobility devices when insurance will not cover the work. If a device cannot be repaired, staff can try to match you with a chair or scooter from the center's reuse program. Funded by San Francisco Department of Disability and Aging Services.
records.next_step: Call the program if you live or work in San Francisco and your mobility device needs repair.
constraints: For people who live or work in San Francisco.
records.phone_note: Vincent Lopez, per the program page

records.name: Mobility 4 Vets Wheelchair Shop
records.description: A volunteer-run nonprofit in Waupaca that repairs and restores wheelchairs and offers them at low cost. It works mainly with veterans but also helps other families who need mobility equipment.
records.next_step: Contact the shop to ask about available chairs and repair help.
constraints: Based on a 2022 news report; confirm hours, location and current services.

records.name: GotDME national directory of equipment lending programs
records.description: A national directory of organizations that lend or accept donated durable medical equipment such as wheelchairs, walkers, hospital beds, rollators, knee scooters and shower safety equipment. It was built because many local loan closets have no website of their own.
records.next_step: Search GotDME for lending programs near you, then call to confirm availability.
constraints: Listings are gathered from the programs themselves; Confirm hours, eligibility and what is in stock before you go.

records.name: Goodwill Medical Equipment Loaner Program
records.description: Lets people borrow a wheelchair or knee scooter at no cost. Goodwill also accepts clean, usable wheelchairs and knee scooters as donations.
records.next_step: Contact Ohio Valley Goodwill about borrowing a wheelchair or knee scooter.
constraints: Serves Greater Cincinnati, so nearby counties may be covered. Confirm your area and current availability.

records.name: Device refurbishing and reutilization program
records.org: YMCA of Central Ohio / ECRN+ with Assistive Technology of Ohio
records.description: ECRN+ accepts donated adaptive equipment, assistive technology and durable medical equipment, and lends equipment in the Columbus area. Loans through the program run up to 90 days.
records.next_step: Call Assistive Technology of Ohio at 1-800-784-3425 or email atohio@osu.edu to ask about borrowing.
constraints: Service area is the Columbus and central Ohio area.
Confirm hours, eligibility and what is in stock before you go.

records.name: Reused and Exchanged Equipment Partnership (REEP)
records.org: Pennsylvania Initiative on Assistive Technology, Temple University
records.description: An online classifieds service that matches people who have unused assistive technology with people who can use it. It is one of the PIAT programs that can be a source of previously owned devices, usually at lower cost than new.
records.next_step: Search REEP for the device you need, or list equipment you no longer use.
constraints: Matches buyers and sellers; condition and price are set by the owner. Confirm hours, eligibility and what is in stock before you go.

records.name: DME Reuse Program
records.description: A center for independent living that runs a durable medical equipment reuse program. It serves people with disabilities and accepts donations from anyone. Listed offices include Jeannette and Pittsburgh.
records.next_step: Call the office nearest you to ask what equipment is available.
constraints: Listed addresses: Jeannette and Pittsburgh. Confirm hours, eligibility and what is in stock before you go.

records.name: Caring Hearts Lending Closet
records.description: A medical lending closet that provides donated, reusable equipment to anyone in need, regardless of financial status. Hours are by appointment.
records.next_step: Call or text 484-463-7603 to make an appointment.
constraints: Appointment only. Large items such as hospital beds and chair lifts may not be accepted.

records.name: A New Start reuse program
records.org: Center for Independent Living of North Central PA
records.description: Accepts donated assistive technology and durable medical equipment in good condition and redistributes it through its reuse program at its Williamsport building. The center is also the local partner for TechOWL, Pennsylvania's assistive technology program.
records.next_step: Contact the center to ask what equipment is available.
constraints: Based in Williamsport. Confirm hours, eligibility and what is in stock before you go.

records.name: UPMC Medical Equipment Recycling Program
records.description: A hospital-system program that collects, refurbishes and distributes medical equipment. UPMC reports more than 15,000 refurbished pieces distributed since the program began in 1999.
records.next_step: Ask UPMC how to request or donate equipment.
constraints: Figure is from a 2019 report. Locations include UPMC Horizon in western Pennsylvania; Confirm hours, eligibility and what is in stock before you go.

records.name: Durable medical equipment loan closets
records.description: Each of the three independent living center locations, Buffalo, Batavia and Niagara Falls, keeps a loan closet of durable medical equipment you can borrow. The agency also accepts donated items.
records.next_step: Contact the location nearest you to ask what is available to borrow.
constraints: The agency may not always be able to pick up donated items. Confirm hours, eligibility and what is in stock before you go.

records.name: California Assistive Technology Reuse Coalition
records.org: Ability Tools (California Assistive Technology Act Program)
records.description: Ability Tools coordinates reuse programs across California that take donated mobility equipment, then clean, repair and provide it free or at low cost. Its NATADS portal lets you search for used equipment from many programs, and its loan program offers $500 to $15,000 for items such as wheelchairs and vehicle modifications.
records.next_step: Search the NATADS portal or choose a reuse program near you on the Ability Tools site.
constraints: Reuse programs set their own eligibility and prices.

records.name: REquipment durable medical equipment reuse
records.org: REquipment DME and AT Reuse Program, Inc.
records.description: Refurbishes and provides free durable medical equipment to adults, children and elders with disabilities in Massachusetts, including power and manual wheelchairs, scooters, adapted strollers, standers, portable ramps and shower chairs.
records.next_step: Contact REquipment to ask about the equipment you need.
constraints: Confirm hours, eligibility and what is in stock before you go.

records.name: Foundation for Rehabilitation Equipment and Endowment (FREE)
records.description: A Virginia nonprofit that collects, cleans, repairs and provides donated mobility and medical equipment to low-income adults and seniors. It reported providing nearly 5,000 devices in 2021.
records.next_step: Contact FREE to ask about borrowing or donating equipment.
constraints: Figure is from a 2022 report. Confirm hours, eligibility and what is in stock before you go.

records.name: Richard West Assistive Technology Advocacy Center
records.description: New Jersey's Assistive Technology Act program. It provides information, device demonstration and lending, advocacy and technical assistance on assistive technology, and runs Back In Action, which puts unused equipment into the hands of someone who can use it.
records.next_step: Call the center to ask about borrowing or trying a device, or to get help with an assistive technology denial.
constraints: Open to people with disabilities, their families and representatives.

records.name: Medical equipment loan ministry
records.description: Lends gently used medical equipment to the public, and you do not need to belong to the church to borrow.
records.next_step: Call 908-396-6057 to ask about available equipment.
constraints: Church-run volunteer program. Confirm hours and what is in stock.

records.name: Maryland Technology Assistance Program (MDTAP)
records.description: Maryland's assistive technology program. It offers device demonstrations, short-term loans, reuse, training and a low-interest loan program for items such as wheelchairs, scooters, vehicles and home modifications. Regional libraries are at Baltimore, the Eastern Shore, Southern Maryland and the centers for independent living.
records.next_step: Call MDTAP or visit mdtap.org to book a demonstration, borrow a device or ask about a loan.
constraints: Loan terms and rates change; confirm current terms with MDTAP.

records.name: Portable ramp loan project
records.org: MDTAP with Maryland centers for independent living
records.description: MDTAP partners with centers for independent living across Maryland to loan portable ramps to people who need a short-term way in and out of a home. Ramps can be loaned for up to four months.
records.next_step: Contact your local center for independent living, or MDTAP, to ask which ramps are available.
constraints: Short-term loan, up to four months. Availability varies by center.

records.name: Maryland Department of Aging Equipment Reuse Program
records.description: Provides sanitized and repaired durable medical equipment at no cost to Marylanders with any illness, injury or disability, regardless of age.
records.next_step: Contact the Maryland Department of Aging to ask how to request equipment.
constraints: Described in an MDTAP presentation. Confirm current process and inventory.

records.name: Maryland Home Modifications Guide
records.description: A state guide to home modification help in Maryland. It lists programs such as Baltimore County BCAUSE, the Housing Accessibility Modification Program, Howard County's renovation program, matching grants through the seven centers for independent living, volunteer groups like Rebuilding Together and Habitat for Humanity, and tips on finding a contractor.
records.next_step: Read the guide, then contact the program in your county.
constraints: Program availability and rules vary by county.

records.name: STAR Program (System of Technology to Achieve Results)
records.description: Minnesota's assistive technology program. It lends medical equipment and assistive technology at no cost for a set loan period, runs demonstrations and reuse services, and serves people of all ages. No proof of disability is required.
records.next_step: Call or email STAR to borrow a device or find used equipment.
constraints: Loans are time-limited; short-term loans are 45 days or less.

records.name: Emergency and Accessibility Loan Program
records.description: Helps low-income homeowners pay for accessibility needs of a household member with a disability, or for emergency repairs. The maximum loan is $27,000.
records.next_step: Ask Minnesota Housing or your local Rehabilitation Loan administrator how to apply.
constraints: Requires meeting income limits, owning and living in the home, and keeping taxes and mortgage current.
Summary from a home-modification research center; confirm current limits.

records.name: Reuse and device loan programs
records.org: Access North Center for Independent Living
records.description: An independent living center that runs assistive technology demonstration and device loans and a reuse and recycle program for northeastern Minnesota.
records.next_step: Call the Duluth office at (888) 625-1401 or the Hibbing office at (800) 390-3681.
constraints: Confirm what equipment is available.

records.name: WisTech
records.description: Wisconsin's assistive technology program. Services are provided through the state's independent living centers and partners, including device demonstration, short-term device loans, and a reuse program that can provide equipment such as a wheelchair.
records.next_step: Contact your local independent living center or the WisTech program.
constraints: Loans are short term, to try equipment or as a loaner.

records.name: WisLoan
records.org: Wisconsin WisTech with independent living centers
records.description: A statewide low-interest loan program for Wisconsin residents with disabilities to buy assistive technology and equipment, make home modifications or adapt a vehicle. Applications go through your local independent living center.
records.next_step: Contact the independent living center that serves your county to apply.
constraints: Open to Wisconsin residents of all ages who have a disability.

records.name: Assistive Technology Program of Colorado
records.org: Center for Inclusive Design and Engineering, University of Colorado
records.description: Colorado's assistive technology act program. It offers device loans, including open-ended loans, technology reuse, demonstrations and information about devices, services and funding.
records.next_step: Visit the program's website to ask about a loan or demonstration.
constraints: Confirm what equipment is available.

records.name: Health First Colorado Home Modification Benefit
records.org: Colorado Department of Health Care Policy and Financing
records.description: A Medicaid long-term services and supports benefit that covers specific home modifications in an eligible person's existing home. A therapist evaluation on the state form is part of the process.
records.next_step: Ask your case manager or community centered board about a home modification request.
constraints: Requires Health First Colorado eligibility and a qualifying waiver or program.
Summary from a home-modification research center; confirm current limits with the state.

records.name: Equipment loan closet and assistive technology (TRAID)
records.description: Short-term loans of durable medical equipment and assistive technology, including wheelchairs, walkers, tub seats and commodes. Some items may be available at no cost when supplies allow. No prescription, referral, payment or documentation is required to borrow.
records.next_step: Call 607-724-2111 and ask for the loan closet (TRAID) coordinator to make an appointment.
constraints: Loans are short term. Appointments are required.
The main office is in Binghamton; satellite offices serve Chenango and Delaware counties.

records.name: NY Connects: free help finding long-term care and disability services
records.description: A free information and assistance service for people of all ages, disabilities and income levels, and for families, caregivers and professionals. STIC delivers NY Connects with the Broome County Office for Aging, the Chenango County Area Agency on Aging and Tioga Opportunities.
records.next_step: Call the Tioga and Chenango contact at (607) 222-1931 or email nyconnects@stic-cil.org.
constraints: Information is offered by phone, or in person if needed.

records.name: Chenango County Area Agency on Aging and NY Connects
records.org: Chenango County Area Agency on Aging
records.description: The county office for older adults and NY Connects, a free service that links people of any age to long-term services and supports. It is in the Chenango County Office Building in Norwich.
records.next_step: Call (607) 337-1770, or visit 5 Court Street, Norwich.
constraints: Confirm hours before visiting.

records.name: Delaware County Office for the Aging loan closet and NY Connects
records.org: Delaware County Office for the Aging
records.description: The office runs a loan closet with wheelchairs, walkers, commodes, crutches and similar equipment for elderly Delaware County clients, and hosts NY Connects for help finding services.
records.next_step: Call the office at 607-832-5750 to ask about equipment.
constraints: Loan closet service is described for elderly clients.

records.name: Otsego County Office for the Aging and NY Connects
records.org: Otsego County Office for the Aging
records.description: The county office for older adults and NY Connects. Its published resource directory includes a section listing loan closets for medical equipment and supplies in the county, with offices in Cooperstown and Oneonta.
records.next_step: Call 607-547-4232 or email nyconnects@otsegocounty.com and ask about loan closets.
constraints: The Oneonta office is by appointment only.

records.name: Ramp It Up wheelchair ramp program
records.org: Broome County Council of Churches (Faith in Action Volunteers)
records.description: Builds wheelchair ramps for homebound Broome County residents with volunteer youth groups and community organizations under skilled mentors. The program is income-based on a sliding scale. Applications are accepted year round, and ramps are built in summer.
records.next_step: Call 607-724-9130 ext. 323 to request an application.
constraints: Ramps are built in summer only, so there may be a wait.

records.name: Medical equipment loan (211 CNY listing)
records.description: Provides durable medical equipment on a short-term loan. Staff will help explore financial assistance if insurance does not cover the cost and the item is not in the loan closet.
records.next_step: Call 315-438-4790 to ask what equipment is available.
constraints: Directory listing; confirm eligibility and what is in stock.

records.name: Open-source mobility equipment and right-to-repair advocacy
records.description: A nonprofit that designs and shares open-source mobility equipment, such as the Endurance power chair and the RozRover for children, built to be repaired, modified and improved by the people who use it. MIF also speaks up for users' right to repair. It is based in Mount Upton, New York.
records.next_step: Visit MIF to read about its designs, ask a question or donate.
constraints: MIF is a nonprofit; designs are for builders and providers, and it does not replace your insurance or clinician.
Mobility Talk's creator serves as MIF's Finance Officer.

records.name: Alabama device reuse centers (walkers, wheelchairs, DME)
records.org: Alabama Department of Rehabilitation Services, APTAT
records.description: Five community partners reuse donated walkers, wheelchairs and other durable medical equipment. Devices are available to Alabama residents regardless of income or disability status. Centers are in Montgomery, Dothan, Homewood, Huntsville and Mobile.
records.next_step: Call the center nearest you to ask what is in stock, or call 1-800-441-7607.
constraints: Stock changes; call first.
Reuse centers do not replace insurance or a clinician's fitting.

records.name: Alabama Ability Loan Program
records.org: Alabama Department of Rehabilitation Services, APTAT
records.description: A low-interest loan for assistive technology, adaptive equipment and related services, run through Alabama's Assistive Technology Act program.
records.next_step: Contact APTAT to ask about eligibility and how to apply.
constraints: It is a loan that must be repaid; terms are set by the lender.

records.name: Connecticut Tech Act Project: device loans, reuse and AT loans
records.description: Connecticut's Assistive Technology Act program offers hands-on device demonstrations, short-term device loans, device recycling and a low-interest assistive technology loan program.
records.next_step: Call 860-803-0588 or 1-800-537-2549, or visit the project's website.
constraints: Check current device availability and loan terms with the program.

records.name: Easterseals Iowa equipment loan and Iowa AT Exchange
records.description: Lends donated durable medical equipment such as hospital beds, wheelchairs and bathroom devices for as long as needed. Also runs a device lending library and a free classified-style exchange for used assistive technology.
records.next_step: Call 1-866-866-8782 or email atinfo@eastersealsia.org to ask about equipment or arrange pickup or shipping.
constraints: Not an emergency program, and it does not repair equipment.
Donated equipment varies in availability.

records.name: LATAN: AT Marketplace reuse, device loans and financial loans
records.description: Louisiana's Assistive Technology Act program runs a reuse marketplace for items such as wheelchairs, walkers and bath chairs, short-term device loans, demonstrations, and loan options for assistive technology and vehicles.
records.next_step: Call 225-925-9500 or visit latan.org to browse the marketplace or ask about a loan.
constraints: Availability varies; ask about eligibility for each service.

records.name: Oklahoma ABLE Tech Device Reutilization Program
records.description: Refurbishes and reassigns gently used durable medical equipment at no cost to Oklahomans, working with the Oklahoma Health Care Authority. SoonerCare members get priority. ABLE Tech also offers short-term device loans and a 5% financial loan program.
records.next_step: Email atreuse@okstate.edu or call 405-967-6010 to ask about available equipment.
constraints: Supply depends on donations.
SoonerCare members are served first.

records.name: Assistive Technology of Alaska: loan, reuse and demonstrations
records.org: Assistive Technology of Alaska (ATLA) for Alaska DVR
records.description: Alaska's statewide assistive technology program connects people to loaned, reused and free or used equipment and holds demonstrations. It also runs the AKTradingPost web exchange. There are no age or income requirements to work with ATLA.
records.next_step: Call (907) 563-2599 or 1-800-723-2852, or email atla@atlaak.org.
constraints: Availability varies; ask what is in stock before travelling.

records.name: iCAN: equipment loans and reuse in Arkansas
records.org: Arkansas Rehabilitation Services, Increasing Capabilities Access Network
records.description: Arkansas's assistive technology program offers free equipment demonstrations, equipment loans and a reuse and recycling program for any Arkansan with a disability or health issue. It also supports a revolving loan fund for assistive technology.
records.next_step: Call 1-800-828-2799 or email info@ar-ican.org to ask about loans or reuse equipment.
constraints: Short loans have set periods; reuse stock varies.

records.name: ATK-KEE Reuse: free refurbished medical equipment in Kansas
records.org: Assistive Technology for Kansans (University of Kansas)
records.description: Eligible Kansans can get refurbished manual and power wheelchairs, patient lifts, hospital beds and shower chairs at no cost. Regional specialists in Oakley, Salina, Topeka, Wichita and Parsons serve all 105 counties. ATK also works with the K-Loan financial loan program.
records.next_step: Call 1-800-526-3648 to reach your regional specialist and ask what is available.
constraints: Eligibility applies; donated stock varies by region.

records.name: New Mexico Technology Assistance Program: device loans and AT loans
records.description: New Mexico's assistive technology program lends devices from a loan bank in Albuquerque, holds demonstrations and offers a financial loan program. It serves people of any disability, age or income anywhere in the state.
records.next_step: Call 505-841-4464 or email nmtap@gcd.nm.gov to ask about a loan or a device trial.
constraints: Device loans are short term and carry a loan agreement.

records.name: Maine CITE and ALLTECH: AT4Maine loans and equipment reuse
records.description: Maine CITE runs the AT4Maine online library of more than 500 devices to borrow. ALLTECH in Portland takes donated walkers, wheelchairs, shower benches and commodes, and offers them at greatly reduced prices or on temporary loan.
records.next_step: Call Maine CITE at 207-621-3195, or ALLTECH at 207-535-2017.
constraints: ALLTECH equipment may carry a low cost; call for stock.

records.name: Nebraska ATP: device loans and ReUse Network
records.description: Nebraska's state assistive technology program demonstrates and loans equipment and runs a ReUse program where donated assistive technology and durable medical equipment is given away at no charge. Offices are in Lincoln, Omaha, Columbus, Kearney and Scottsbluff.
records.next_step: Call (877) 713-4402 or email atp@nebraska.gov, or browse equipment on AT4ALL.
constraints: Loans and services are by appointment; reuse stock varies.

records.name: Mississippi Project START: device loan and reutilization
records.description: Project START lends devices for a short-term trial and refurbishes donated durable medical equipment, giving it free to Mississippians with disabilities or chronic health issues. Its demonstration center and loan library are in Madison.
records.next_step: Call 601-853-5249 or email projectstart@mdrs.ms.gov, and complete the application for services.
constraints: Reuse equipment is for people with no other readily available source.
Loan periods vary by device.

records.name: MonTECH: free equipment loans, reuse exchange and adaptive trikes
records.org: MonTECH, University of Montana Rural Institute
records.description: MonTECH lends assistive devices free for 30, 90 or 180 days and ships most items anywhere in Montana at no charge. It also runs a free reuse exchange, adaptive trike loans in five communities, and a financial loan program with Rural Dynamics.
records.next_step: Call (406) 243-5511 or email montech@mso.umt.edu, or request a loan on the MonTECH site.
constraints: Exchange listings are between buyers and sellers directly.

records.name: ATinNH: loans, demonstrations and equipment reuse
records.org: Assistive Technology in New Hampshire, UNH Institute on Disability
records.description: ATinNH runs a refurbish and reuse network with partners that offer long-term loans of donated equipment, such as the Chapin Senior Center in New London. AT4All NH lists equipment for loan, demonstration and reuse.
records.next_step: Call 603-397-7251 or email nh.at4all@unh.edu, or browse the AT4All NH database.
constraints: Availability varies and inventories change often.

records.name: Wyoming Assistive Technology Resources: loans and reuse
records.org: Wyoming Institute for Disabilities, University of Wyoming
records.description: WATR lends a wide variety of assistive devices to Wyoming residents and runs a reuse program where lightly used devices and durable medical equipment can be exchanged, bought or donated. Listings are on Wyoming AT4ALL.
records.next_step: Fill out the device loan request form, or call (307) 766-6187 or email watr@uwyo.edu.
constraints: Reuse items may carry a modest price; check each listing.

records.name: Rhode Island Assistive Technology Access Partnership (ATAP)
records.org: RI Office of Rehabilitation Services with TechACCESS of RI and OSCIL
records.description: ATAP is a statewide partnership offering device demonstrations, equipment loans and reuse of items such as hospital beds. Partners include TechACCESS of RI and the Ocean State Center for Independent Living.
records.next_step: Visit the ATAP page to find the partner for your need.
constraints: Some partner programs, such as the telephone equipment loan, have eligibility rules.

records.name: Delaware Assistive Technology Initiative (DATI): loans and AT Exchange
records.description: DATI's Assistive Technology Resource Centers in Newark and Milford offer no-cost equipment demonstrations and short-term loans. Its AT Exchange lets people buy, sell or give away used devices through want ads.
records.next_step: Call 800-870-3284 or email dati-ud@udel.edu, and contact your local resource center before visiting.
constraints: Loans are short-term for trial use; call ahead.

records.name: Assistive Technology Resource Centers of Hawaii: loan bank and AT Exchange
records.org: Assistive Technology Resource Centers of Hawaii (ATRC)
records.description: ATRC lends assistive technology free of charge, runs equipment loan banks, an AT Exchange for trading or donating devices in good working order, and a low-interest financial loan program.
records.next_step: Call (808) 532-7110 or 1-800-645-3007, or email info@atrc.org to reserve a device.
constraints: Devices must be returned after the trial period.

records.name: Idaho Assistive Technology Project: reuse, lending library and AT4All
records.org: Idaho Assistive Technology Project, University of Idaho
records.description: IATP's Reuse program provides new and gently used assistive technology and durable medical equipment at no cost to people of all ages with disabilities who cannot afford to buy new. Recipients may keep equipment as long as needed. Idaho AT4All lists equipment for sale, loan or free.
records.next_step: Call 1-800-432-8324 or email idahoat@uidaho.edu to ask about reuse equipment.
constraints: Demand exceeds inventory; ask to be matched when equipment arrives.

records.name: Nevada AT Collaborative and CARE Chest: reuse and open-ended loans
records.org: Nevada Assistive Technology Collaborative with CARE Chest of Sierra Nevada
records.description: CARE Chest of Sierra Nevada accepts gently used equipment, sanitizes and repairs it, and reassigns it by open-ended loan, including wheelchairs, shower chairs, walkers and canes. The Nevada AT Resource Centers also lend devices for short-term trials in Las Vegas and Reno.
records.next_step: Call the Nevada AT Resource Center at 775-682-9070 (north) or (702) 780-4113 (south), or contact CARE Chest.
constraints: Available equipment depends on donations.

records.name: North Dakota Assistive: equipment trial loans and AT4All reuse
records.description: North Dakota Assistive offers a short-term equipment trial program and an AT4All site where devices are listed for sale, giveaway, demonstration or loan. It also runs a financial loan program.
records.next_step: Call 800-895-4728 or email info@ndassistive.org.
constraints: Trial loans are short-term; reuse listings are posted by many sources.

records.name: DakotaLink: Medical Equipment Recycle and Reuse (MERR) and loans
records.org: DakotaLink, South Dakota Assistive Technology Program
records.description: MERR makes wheelchairs, scooters, standers, patient lifts, gait trainers and hospital beds available at no cost to South Dakota Medicaid recipients, and for a nominal fee to others. DakotaLink also offers device loans and a financial loan fund.
records.next_step: Call MERR at 605-271-5074 or 1-866-274-2594, or email Merrinfo@dakotalink.net.
constraints: Non-Medicaid recipients pay a nominal fee.

records.name: Vermont Assistive Technology Program: loans and AT Exchange
records.description: Vermont's program offers hands-on equipment demonstrations, device loans and a free peer-to-peer used equipment exchange at vt.at4all.com.
records.next_step: Call 1-800-750-6355 or email dail.atinfo@vermont.gov.
constraints: Exchange sales are between buyers and sellers.

records.name: DC SHARES and DC Assistive Technology Program
records.org: DC Assistive Technology Program (University Legal Services)
records.description: DC SHARES collects and distributes used manual wheelchairs, walkers, lifts, crutches, canes, commodes and shower chairs free to DC residents. The DC Assistive Technology Program also runs a device loan library, a cane and walker clinic and a financing loan program.
records.next_step: Call the DC Assistive Technology Program at (202) 547-0198.
constraints: Powered equipment is generally not collected; ask about availability.

records.name: Project MEND: refurbished wheelchairs and medical equipment (San Antonio)
records.description: A nonprofit that collects donated medical equipment, then repairs, sanitizes and refurbishes it for people in need, including wheelchairs and power chairs. It focuses on veterans with support from the Texas Veterans Commission and is a demonstration center for the Texas Technology Access Program.
records.next_step: Ask your therapist or doctor for a referral, or contact Project MEND through the Texas Technology Access Program at 1-800-828-7839.
constraints: Based in San Antonio; ask about service area and wait times.

records.name: Texas reuse programs listed by TTAP (Houston, El Paso, Austin)
records.description: The Texas Technology Access Program lists medical equipment reuse programs in Houston (RSVP Texas, Medical Bridges), El Paso (Project C.A.R.E.) and Austin (CPath). TTAP also lends devices for 35 days with shipping included.
records.next_step: Call TTAP at (512) 232-0740 or 1-800-828-7839 for referrals and device loans.
constraints: These reuse programs are not sponsored by TTAP; confirm eligibility with each.

records.name: FAAST Regional Reuse Centers and AT Exchange (Florida)
records.org: Florida Alliance for Assistive Services and Technology
records.description: FAAST funds five Regional Reuse Centers at select Centers for Independent Living. They accept donated equipment, clean, repair and refurbish it, and return it to the community at no cost. FAAST also runs an online AT Exchange and short-term device loans through regional demonstration centers.
records.next_step: Call FAAST at (850) 487-2378 or email info@faast.org to find the reuse center near you.
constraints: Equipment depends on donations; call the center first.

records.name: ARISE and Exceptional Family Resources: loan closet and free ramps
records.description: ARISE runs a medical equipment loan closet with a wide range of equipment families can borrow free short term, and builds and installs free modular wheelchair ramps for eligible people. It also creates custom low-cost adaptive equipment.
records.next_step: Call 315-472-3171 in Syracuse, or Cayuga and Seneca at 315-671-4651, or Oswego at 315-602-4938.
constraints: Ramps are for eligible individuals; ask about the application.

records.name: ALS Association loan closets: Albany, Buffalo, Rochester, Syracuse
records.org: ALS Association (Robert Wright Memorial Equipment Loan Program)
records.description: Provides durable medical equipment and communication aids on loan to people living with ALS, using donated and new equipment, through loan closets in Albany, Buffalo, Rochester and Syracuse.
records.next_step: Contact the ALS Association chapter to register and request equipment.
constraints: For people living with ALS.

records.name: Ulster County medical equipment loan closet
records.org: Ulster County Office for the Aging (RCAL)
records.description: Lends donated medical equipment to people who cannot afford to buy their own or whose insurance does not cover it. The usual loan is three months and can be extended. A fee applies for some items.
records.next_step: Call 845-331-0541 to check what is available and make an appointment.
constraints: Fee prices changed July 1, 2024; ask when you call.

records.name: Suffolk County TRAID loan: equipment at no cost (SILO)
records.org: Suffolk Independent Living Organization with NYS Justice Center
records.description: SILO partners with the New York State Justice Center to loan durable medical equipment and assistive devices free. A treating professional's documentation is required.
records.next_step: Contact SILO through the Suffolk County Assistive Technology Advocacy Project.
constraints: Documentation from a doctor, PT or OT is required.

records.name: Tri-County Independent Living Center loan closet
records.description: Lends donated mobility, medical and home modification equipment for temporary use by people with disabilities. Inventory depends on donations and returns.
records.next_step: Contact the center to ask what is in the loan closet.
constraints: The center does not buy equipment; inventory changes.

records.name: Church of the Ascension Medical Loan Closet (Johnstown)
records.description: Loans medical equipment such as wheelchairs and medical beds to anyone for free.
records.next_step: Call (614) 581-5286 or (740) 390-8048 to check availability.
constraints: Volunteer run; call first.

records.name: Jefferson County free ramp program
records.description: A volunteer program that builds handicap ramps for Jefferson County residents at no cost.
records.next_step: Call United Way of Jefferson County at 740-284-9000.
constraints: Availability depends on volunteers and materials.

records.name: Veterans Miracle Center Erie: ramps for veterans
records.description: Offers handicap ramps to disabled veterans who meet DD-214 and income requirements, free of charge, with donations welcome. Open Tuesday through Thursday, 10 am to 2 pm, or by appointment.
records.next_step: Call to ask about an application.
constraints: Veterans only; DD-214 and income requirements apply.

records.name: ReCARES: weekly durable medical equipment donations and loans (Bay Area)
records.description: A nonprofit whose volunteers gather weekly in Oakland, San Francisco and Marin to accept donations of durable medical equipment and supplies for people in need.
records.next_step: Check the ReCARES site for site hours and equipment.
constraints: Check availability and eligibility before visiting.

records.name: Renew Mobility: donated mobility equipment and free repair pop-ups
records.description: West Michigan nonprofit that takes donated, gently used mobility equipment and has held free repair days for walkers, manual wheelchairs, bath equipment, canes and cushions.
records.next_step: Contact Renew Mobility about equipment availability and the next repair day.
constraints: On-site power wheelchair repair was not offered at the pop-up event reported.
Check eligibility and availability.

records.name: disAbility Connections: equipment repair shop and power chair storage
records.description: Independent living center in Jackson that runs a shop for durable medical equipment repair and stores power wheelchairs and scooters.
records.next_step: Call the center to ask about equipment and repair services.
constraints: Details taken from a volunteer listing; confirm services directly.

records.name: SOS International free wheelchair repair clinics (Louisville)
records.description: Nonprofit that has run volunteer wheelchair repair clinics in Louisville, including for residents of public housing and people who are unhoused.
records.next_step: Check SOS International for the next clinic date.
constraints: Clinics are periodic; reported in 2024 news coverage.

records.name: Stout Vocational Rehabilitation Institute free wheelchair clinics
records.description: University program that has offered free clinics to check, repair and clean wheelchairs.
records.next_step: Check UW-Stout SVRI for clinic dates.
constraints: Clinics held on set dates; confirm the schedule.

records.name: Wheelchair Foundation: manual wheelchairs for people in need in the U.S.
records.description: Provides standard manual wheelchairs to qualified people in the United States who show financial need. Applicants submit an application, a waiver and a brief medical recommendation.
records.next_step: Email info@wheelchairfoundation.org for the application packet.
constraints: Manual wheelchairs only; does not accept physical wheelchair donations.

records.name: Brooks Temporary Loan Closet (with CIL Jacksonville)
records.description: Free temporary loans of durable medical equipment, including manual and electric wheelchairs, walkers, canes, crutches and shower equipment. Short-term and long-term loans are available.
records.next_step: Use the request form on the Brooks TLC page.
constraints: Serves residents of the five listed counties.

records.name: Manatee County Community Paramedicine Lending Library
records.description: County program that lends donated health and mobility equipment with no time limit and accepts donated equipment at its Bradenton office.
records.next_step: Contact Manatee County Community Health about available equipment.
constraints: Does not accept broken equipment, hospital beds or other large furniture.

records.name: West Shore Senior Center loan closet (Cumberland County)
records.description: Free loans of wheelchairs, walkers, crutches, canes and commode chairs. Open to West Shore and Eastern Cumberland County residents, not only seniors.
records.next_step: Call for hours and availability.
constraints: Intake requires a West Shore, Eastern Cumberland or New Cumberland address.

records.name: Dauphin County Area Agency on Aging loan closet
records.org: Dauphin County Area Agency on Aging
records.description: Free loan closet at the county administration building in Harrisburg for senior adults living in Dauphin County.
records.next_step: Call the Area Agency on Aging to ask what is on hand.
constraints: Listed for Dauphin County seniors; confirm eligibility.

records.name: Camp Hill Borough medical equipment loan program
records.description: Two-month loans of wheelchairs, quad canes, walkers, portable toilets and shower seats, free of charge, for Camp Hill Borough residents.
records.next_step: Call the borough office for availability.
constraints: Camp Hill Borough residents only.
Loan period is two months.

records.name: Jewish Family Service durable medical equipment loan closet (Lancaster)
records.description: Lends wheelchairs, walkers, canes, shower stools and bedside commodes to anyone in need. Equipment is returned when no longer needed so others can use it.
records.next_step: Visit during open hours at Congregation Shaarai Shomayim.
constraints: Open Monday 10-12 and Wednesday 9-11 except Jewish holidays; confirm before visiting.

records.name: Reagan's Journey pediatric equipment lending closet
records.description: Free pediatric medical equipment and supply lending closet in Lancaster.
records.next_step: Contact the program to make an appointment.
constraints: By appointment only.

records.name: Hiland Presbyterian Church durable medical equipment lending closet
records.description: Church-run lending closet in Pittsburgh for Allegheny County residents; it also manages a Hospital Equipment Loan Plan.
records.next_step: Visit during open hours.
constraints: Allegheny County residents; you must be able to pick up the equipment.
Open Monday-Thursday 10-2; confirm before visiting.

records.name: Blessing Board: free durable medical equipment (Shaler)
records.description: Nonprofit that collects durable medical equipment and gives it to people in need in Allegheny and surrounding counties.
records.next_step: Contact Blessing Board about available equipment.
constraints: Reported in news coverage; confirm current service area.

records.name: Rebuilding Together Houston wheelchair ramp and veterans repair programs
records.description: Free wheelchair ramps for qualifying homeowners across Harris County, plus a veterans repair program funded by a Texas Veterans Commission grant.
records.next_step: Email intake@rebuildinghouston.org or call (713) 659-2511.
constraints: Low-income homeowner listed on the deed and living in the home full time.

records.name: Wheels of Hope: wheelchair distribution (Canton)
records.description: Distributes wheelchairs to people who do not have one and seeks donated wheelchairs.
records.next_step: Contact Wheels of Hope for eligibility and availability.
constraints: Listed in directories; confirm current operations.

records.name: United Spinal Association peer support: mentoring and support groups
records.description: One-on-one peer mentoring plus virtual and in-person support group meetings for people with spinal cord injuries and all wheelchair users. Chapters operate nationwide, and membership is free.
records.next_step: Open the peer support page to request a mentor or find a group.
constraints: Chapter and group availability varies by area.

records.name: Reeve Foundation Peer & Family Support Program
records.description: Matches people affected by paralysis with certified peer mentors, and offers virtual support groups for caregivers, people with quadriplegia and people with paraplegia.
records.next_step: Call the Reeve Foundation or use the peer program page to request a mentor.
constraints: Groups are virtual; check the current schedule.

records.name: Amputee Coalition: support groups and certified peer visitors
records.description: Runs a national network of 300+ registered support groups, certified peer visitors who meet with people and families in person, by phone or online, and monthly virtual groups. Services are free.
records.next_step: Search the support group finder by zip code or request a peer visit.
constraints: Registered local groups are run by volunteers, not by the Coalition; confirm meeting details before attending.

records.name: Bay Area Spinal Cord Injury Peer Group (Berkeley)
records.description: Peer group for people with spinal cord injury that meets at the Ed Roberts Campus in Berkeley.
records.next_step: Check the group's Facebook page for meeting details.
constraints: Listed in a Reeve Foundation resource sheet; confirm meeting times.

records.name: Helen Hayes Hospital spinal cord and amputee support group
records.description: Hospital-hosted support group for people with spinal cord injury and amputation in West Haverstraw.
records.next_step: Contact the hospital for meeting times.
constraints: Listed in the United Spinal group network; confirm schedule.

records.name: UPMC spinal cord injury peer support group (Pittsburgh)
records.description: Spinal cord injury peer support group hosted at UPMC Mercy in Pittsburgh.
records.next_step: Contact UPMC rehabilitation for the schedule.
constraints: Listed in the United Spinal group network; confirm schedule.

records.name: Spinal Cord Support Group of Hummelstown
records.org: Spinal Cord Support Group of Hummelstown
records.description: Local spinal cord injury support group listed in the United Spinal network.
records.next_step: Open the United Spinal group listing for contact details.
constraints: Confirm that the group is still meeting.

records.name: Spinal Cord Injury Peer Support Group (Austin)
records.description: Peer support group for people with spinal cord injury in Austin, listed in the United Spinal network.
records.next_step: Open the United Spinal group listing for contact details.
constraints: Confirm meeting times.

records.name: Baylor Institute for Rehabilitation spinal cord injury peer group (Dallas)
records.description: Spinal cord injury peer group listed at Baylor Institute for Rehabilitation in Dallas.
records.next_step: Open the United Spinal group listing for contact details.
constraints: Confirm meeting times.

records.name: Rehabilitation Institute of Michigan spinal cord injury support group (Detroit)

records.name: Servants at Work (SAWs): free wheelchair ramps
records.description: Faith-based volunteer nonprofit that builds ADA-compliant wooden wheelchair ramps for people with permanent or long-term disabilities in low-income households. It covers 70 of Indiana's 92 counties and partners with other ramp builders elsewhere.
records.next_step: Apply through the SAWs website or call to ask about your county.
constraints: Low-income households; check your county is covered.
Waiting lists vary.

records.name: RAMP UP Indiana (IHCDA grants to ramp builders)
records.org: Indiana Housing and Community Development Authority
records.description: State program that gives grants to nonprofits to install exterior ramps for low-income homeowners at or below 80% of area median income. It funds ramp builders, not individuals.
records.next_step: Ask a local ramp nonprofit or Area Agency on Aging whether it receives RAMP UP funds; questions go to rampup@ihcda.in.gov.
constraints: Homeowners at or below 80% of area median income.
Applications are by nonprofits; check that the program is open.

records.name: SAWs Virginia: volunteer-built wheelchair ramps (Fredericksburg area)
records.description: Virginia affiliate of the national SAWs ramp ministry. Builds wheelchair ramps at no fee for people with disabilities who cannot afford them.
records.next_step: Email virginia@sawsramps.org or visit the website for a consultation.
constraints: Income limits apply (percent of area median income).

records.name: project:HOMES wheelchair ramps and Renew Crew repairs (Richmond area)
records.description: Privately funded volunteer program that builds and installs wheelchair ramps and does accessibility repairs for low-income elderly and disabled homeowners at no charge.
records.next_step: Call the 24-hour hotline at (804) 458-2840.
constraints: Low-income homeowners; confirm that your county is covered.

records.name: RampsRVA (Ramp Access Made Possible by Students)
records.description: Student-founded nonprofit that installs free modular wheelchair ramps for financially qualified older adults and disabled people. Eligibility is based on HUD income guidelines.
records.next_step: Apply through RampsRVA.
constraints: Must be elderly or disabled and low-income by HUD guidelines.

records.name: RampsAcrossAmerica: free ramps in Hampton Roads
records.description: Builds free ADA-accessible wheelchair ramps for people of any age who cannot enter their home and cannot afford a ramp. Income is based on household income. It serves the Hampton Roads area.
records.next_step: Contact RampsAcrossAmerica to apply.
constraints: Hampton Roads area only; the county list on the source covers Virginia Beach, so confirm your city.

records.name: WILS ramp construction program (Warrensburg area)
records.description: Independent living center program that designs and builds ADA wheelchair ramps and hand rails with volunteers and local contractors, using charitable funding where eligible.
records.next_step: Apply to WILS; you may be placed on a waitlist.
constraints: Builds are on hold when funding runs out; applicants go on a waitlist.
Must live in the six-county service area.

records.name: Springfield Center for Independent Living wheelchair ramp program
records.description: Administers a free wheelchair ramp program for renters or homeowners who meet federal poverty guidelines in the city of Springfield.
records.next_step: Call the center for an application.
constraints: May require a waiting list.
Poverty guidelines apply.

records.name: Rampathon: free ramps for homeowners in King and Snohomish counties
records.org: Master Builders Association of King and Snohomish Counties
records.description: Annual volunteer program that builds free wheelchair access ramps for homeowners in need. Applications open each spring.
records.next_step: Watch for the application window on the MBA Rampathon page.
constraints: Annual cycle; applications have closed by May in past years.

records.name: Home Builders Foundation Blitz Build ramps (Denver metro)
records.description: Annual Blitz Build in which volunteers build mobility ramps for free around the Denver metro area, paid for by sponsors and donated materials.
records.next_step: Contact the Home Builders Foundation about applying.
constraints: Reported in news coverage; the metro county list is not published in the source.

records.name: Stavros Home Sweet Home: ramps and equipment (Western Massachusetts)

constraints: Confirm that the program is accepting applications.

records.name: Developmental Disabilities Resource Center (DDRC): Community Centered Board
records.description: Designated Community Centered Board for Jefferson, Clear Creek, Gilpin and Summit counties. It determines developmental disability eligibility and funding routes for children and adults. Case management for the Medicaid waivers in Jefferson and Clear Creek counties moved to Jefferson County Human Services in 2024.
records.next_step: Call DDRC to ask about a developmental disability determination, and ask who provides case management in your county now.
constraints: Eligibility is for qualifying developmental disabilities.
records.phone_note: DDRC main line, from the state case management directory

records.name: Developmental Pathways: Community Centered Board and case management agency
records.description: Community Centered Board for Arapahoe and Douglas counties and the part of Adams County inside Aurora city limits. It determines eligibility and provides programs for people with developmental disabilities, and serves as a case management agency for the HCBS waivers.
records.next_step: Call and ask for an intake coordinator to start an eligibility determination.
constraints: In Adams County this covers only the city of Aurora.
records.phone_note: Case management agency line, from the state directory

records.name: Imagine!: direct services provider for Boulder and Broomfield
records.description: Imagine! provides direct services for people with developmental disabilities, including adult day services, school-age programs and residential services. Since July 1, 2024, case management and waiver intake for Boulder, Broomfield and Gilpin counties are handled by A&I Avenues, which is a separate agency.
records.next_step: Call A&I Avenues about waiver funding and eligibility, and Imagine! about services.

records.name: Colorado Community Centered Boards and case management agencies (statewide directory)
records.org: Colorado Department of Health Care Policy & Financing
records.description: Colorado has one case management agency (CMA) for each of 20 service areas, and these agencies handle intake, eligibility and case management for the developmental disability waivers. Community Centered Boards still provide services. The state directory lists the agency and phone for each county.
records.next_step: Find your county in the directory, then call the case management agency listed for it.

records.name: Michigan Community Mental Health Services Programs (CMHSPs)

records.description: Specialty behavioral health services for people with developmental disabilities are delivered through county-based Community Mental Health Services Programs. Each county has a CMHSP (some serve several counties) that handles intake and service planning.
records.next_step: Use the state CMHSP list to find the program for your county, then call and ask for developmental disability services intake.

records.name: Utah Division of Services for People with Disabilities (DSPD)

records.description: State division that oversees home and community-based services for Utahns with disabilities. Call the intake line to ask about eligibility, the waiting list and services.
records.next_step: Call 1-844-ASK-DSPD and ask about eligibility and how to apply for services.
constraints: Eligibility is for qualifying disabilities and there can be a waiting list.

records.name: Illinois developmental disability services: find your ISC agency
